predecessors.note: The Red Army occupied Lithuania on 16 June 1940; the People's Seimas declared on 21 July 1940 that the Lithuanian people desired to join the Soviet Union.

land.text: Cliopatria's Republic of Lithuania of 1990 (65,346 km2)

successors.note: Declared independence on 11 March 1990 under its pre-1940 name, the Republic of Lithuania.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 74,858 km2 against the infobox 65,200 km2 for 1989 (ratio 0.87; the gazetteer overcounts Lithuania) and Cliopatria's Republic of Lithuania of 1990 (65,346 km2): Lithuania in the borders of 1990. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Lithuania ends in 1939 and has no shape for 1940-1989; the Soviet years lie inside its Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes. The page is silent on the Vilnius and Klaipeda regions and says only "minor adjustments to its border with Belarus"; the lands of 1940 are therefore drawn as the 1990 borders.

ledger.note: 1940, 21 July: "the new People's Seimas declared that the Lithuanian people desired to join the Soviet Union" after the Red Army occupation of 16 June 1940; "On 3 August, a Lithuanian delegation ... was dispatched to Moscow to sign the document".
1941, 22 June: "Nazi Germany invaded the USSR and occupied all of Lithuania within a month."
1944, July to October: "the Red Army entered Lithuania once again" (infobox: SSR re-established September-November 1944). The page gives no single date; October is the end of the window.
1990, 11 March: Lithuania "declared independence from the Soviet Union on 11 March 1990 under its pre-1940 name, the Republic of Lithuania".

certainty.note: The page gives no border changes; Vilnius and Klaipeda lines and the Belarus adjustments are undated.

sources.title: Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 16 June 1940 occupation, 21 July People's Seimas, 3 August delegation; 22 June 1941; July-October 1944; 11 March 1990; area 65,200 km2 (1989); capital Vilnius; silent on Vilnius and Klaipeda.

notes: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Lithuania (1919-1939) and Republic of Lithuania (1990-) bracket the Soviet years; those years lie inside Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes. The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union. Not on the page: the transfer of Vilnius in October 1939 (the page only says the Soviets threatened that Vilnius "could be annexed to Belarus" and names the 10 October 1939 mutual assistance agreement), the Klaipeda Region, the dates of the minor Belarus border adjustments. The 1940-1990 keyframe is the 1990 shape. The 1990 end is the declaration of 11 March 1990, which matches Cliopatria's Republic of Lithuania starting in 1990. The short-lived Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic of 1918-1919 (merged into the Lithuanian-Belorussian SSR; a counterpart string in the Byelorussian SSR dossier) is a different state with the same name. Counterparts: kingdom-of-lithuania and republic-of-lithuania exist (Cliopatria); nazi-germany is a Cliopatria polity.
